item.title: Doctor’s coat takes backseat as Maha’s Vedika Magar chases cricket dreams for Sikkim
item.description: MUMBAI: Not many would give up a settled career, especially one as a doctor, to pursue a sporting dream. Vedika Magar did just that to follow her passion for cricket. Last month, she took her first step towards realising that dream when she represented Sikkim in the Senior Women’s T20 Trophy. Her next target is to play for Mumbai. She has featured on the state’s probables list for the past three seasons but is yet to make the Mumbai 15. Vedika had always wanted to be a cricketer. However, lack of facilities in her hometown of Pandharpur meant that her opportunities were limited to playing tennis-ball cricket with boys in her neighbourhood. When it came to choosing between an engineering seat in Pune and a medical seat in Mumbai, she opted for the latter and enrolled at Grant Medical College. She arrived in Mumbai at 17, fell in love with the city and rediscovered her passion for cricket. In college, she first bowled with a leather ball while practising with the boys’ team. She later began training at the nets of the late Vidya Paradkar, a well-known coach on Mumbai’s maidans, at Cross Maidan. It was only after completing her internship that she was encouraged to take cricket seriously. “Dr Hemant Gupta, who worked in the department of medicine at JJ Hospital, saw me play and was impressed. He was the one who helped me find a club in the city,” the 26-yearold said. At 23, Vedika put her plans for postgraduate studies on hold and took up a job at JJ Hospital to continue her cricketing journey. Her efforts paid off when she made Mumbai’s list of 30 probables for the first time in 2024. “Juggling night shifts, training and matches took a toll on me. I had calcium deficiency and my health deteriorated,” recalls the left-arm spinner. She eventually had to choose between her job and cricket. This time, with her parents’ support, she chose the game.She also landed a role as team doctor with Delhi Capitals’ Women’s Premier League (WPL) outfit. The job helped her manage her expenses while giving her an opportunity to interact with top players and observe their preparation. But progress on the field remained elusive. Then, while browsing the web, she came across an advertisement for open trials for Sikkim. She decided to give it a shot and was rewarded with selection.

item.title: Spurs set to play at Dallas in NBA Cup quarterfinals
item.description: San Antonio Spurs guard Stephon Castle (5) celebrates after scoring a three-pointer in an NBA Cup game against the Los Angeles Lakers at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas on Friday, Nov. 27, 2026. The Spurs defeated the Lakers 99-96. (Katina Zentz/San Antonio Express-News) The Spurs stressed at the start of NBA Cup play they wanted to win the in-season tournament after falling short in the championship game last season in Las Vegas. "We feel like we want to get our 'get-back,' " said forward Devin Vassell, referring to the 124-113 loss to the New York Knicks in the championship game last December. "We have our eyes on the prize, for sure." After overcoming a 20-point deficit to down the Los Angeles Lakers 99-96 on Friday night , the Spurs are one step closer to achieving that goal. The NBA announced after the game the Spurs will face the Dallas Mavericks at 8:30 p.m. on Dec. 4 in Dallas in the quarterfinals, with Prime set to broadcast. The league also announced the Spurs' home game against Toronto set for Dec. 3 has been moved to Dec. 2. The start time for that one is 7 p.m. "We want to win it. It's as simple as that," Spurs guard De'Aaron Fox, who had 12 points and five rebounds Friday night, said of the Cup trophy that eluded them last year. "You put any objective or any goal in front of us and we want to achieve it." Spurs star Victor Wembanyama, who had 25 points and 16 rebounds against the Lakers, agreed. "It's meaningful, for sure," he said of advancing to the knockout round. "Every game. We need to win every game." Subscribe There’s more to San Antonio with the Express-News. item.title: Liverpool ready to battle to sign Bundesliga midfielder
item.description: Liverpool ready to battle to sign Bundesliga midfielder Liverpool transfer interest grows as Wael Mohya emerges as a summer market target Liverpool are among the clubs tracking Borussia Monchengladbach teenager Wael Mohya, with the 17-year-old German playmaker shaping up as one of the most intriguing young names to watch heading into the summer window. According to talkSPORT , Bayern Munich, Brighton and Barcelona are also credited with interest, a detail that immediately points to the level of competition any suitor is likely to face. Mohya’s rise has come against a difficult backdrop. Borussia Monchengladbach have endured a miserable Bundesliga campaign and, as reported, sit rooted to the bottom with only one league win all season. In that environment, young players can often be overwhelmed. Mohya has done the opposite. He has stepped in, handled senior football and contributed two goals in eight appearances, underlining why his name is now travelling so quickly across Europe. Wael Mohya making an impact in Germany There is already a sense that Mohya’s emergence is about more than numbers. He has also been recognised at international level after being named in the latest Germany squad, another marker of how highly he is regarded. He did not feature, but the selection alone signals serious belief in his potential. The player himself has attempted to dampen the noise. Mohya said: “If there were interest, it would be nice recognition of my performances, but nothing more than that. Just let me play football.” It is a measured response and one that suggests a teenager focused on development rather than headlines. That calm stance may be tested if Borussia Monchengladbach are relegated. Should that happen, the pressure to sell prized assets will inevitably increase. For interested clubs, that could create a rare opening to move for a talent before his valuation climbs even further. Photo: IMAGO Liverpool face Bayern Munich competition The expectation from those close to the German game is that the chase could quickly intensify. Andy Brassell told talkSPORT.com: “I think the fact that Mohya has been able to make an impression shows what an enormous personality he’s got.” That point matters. Scouts will always assess technique, output and tactical profile, but mentality is often what separates a promising youngster from a future elite operator. Brassell added: “He’s braver on the ball than a lot of his teammates. He wants to get the ball, he wants to take guys on, he wants to shoot.” It is easy to see why that description would appeal to recruitment departments across Europe, particularly clubs seeking creativity between the lines and confidence in tight spaces. He went further, saying: “Straight away it’s clear that he’s a pretty special talent.” In the current market, those judgments can accelerate quickly from admiration to active pursuit, especially when elite clubs sense a chance to act before a player becomes unattainable. He apologized for the interview and Alonso said the matter was closed, but visiting supporters at the City Ground were less forgiving on a night which saw him substituted after he gave away a penalty. item.title: The ‘extra spice’ fuelling France vs South Africa showdown in Nations Championship final
item.description: It is, in the words of a rival head coach, a “fitting final”. Andy Farrell did not hide his disappointment that Ireland did not make the inaugural Nations Championship showpiece but he did not dispute that France and South Africa were worthy combatants for the trophy. Asked to assess their relative strengths and make a prediction following his side’s win over Australia , the Ireland head coach spent several minutes explaining what makes each so good before eventually suggesting it was too close to call. “But isn’t that how it should be?” Farrell asked – indeed, Andy, indeed. This format clearly has its challenges but there is hope of a dazzling denouement. These are the reigning champions of the northern and southern hemispheres, however distant the Springboks ’ success in last year’s Rugby Championship now feels. Their recent encounter of fine margins in Paris has only deepened a rivalry that has festered in the last half-decade. “I find that it's a good challenge to play them twice in a row knowing that we have already beaten them the first time,” the France lock Florian Verhaeghe said. “That adds a little extra spice.” Florian Verhaeghe believes there will be ‘extra spice’ in the final (Getty) France, by rights, should not really be here. As detailed previously , they were more ambivalent than most towards the Nations Championship, with the July Test window generally considered secondary to the Top 14 climax that almost directly precedes it. Though Bordeaux Begles’ surprise failure to make the play-offs bolstered his options somewhat, head coach Fabien Galthie was still without a raft of regulars for fixtures against New Zealand, Australia and Japan in the first phase of this tournament; to come away with 12 competition points, including a pivotal two losing bonus points against the All Blacks, was outstanding. A few top coaches have wondered if this competition makes it harder to blood players, but both France and South Africa have managed to develop depth while winning. The late-blooming lock Verhaeghe – long of limb and deft of hand – is a great example, seizing his opportunity in the summer and then starting throughout this November campaign. Kalvin Gourgues, meanwhile, has carried through his Toulouse form over the last couple of years into the French side as a bundling ball of energy and point of difference in midfield. France are back at closer to full strength (Getty) Even allowing for a few absentees, this French side looks far stronger than when these teams last met a fortnight ago. There will be no trickery with twin scrum halves, with Matthieu Jalibert and Thomas Ramos returning to join Antoine Dupont in probably the world’s best playmaking spine. “We had other options, but this was an obvious decision,” Galthie said of Ramos’ immediate return following injury. The Springboks, for their part, have talked this week of their excitement to take on a French side at closer to full-strength. A side that knows a thing or two about finals

item.title: 100% wear in 15 laps – F1’s tyre challenges in Qatar far more extreme than Pirelli expected
item.description: Motorsport photo Every year, the Lusail International Circuit represents the biggest challenge on the Formula 1 calendar for its sole tyre supplier, Pirelli. It is precisely for that reason that a maximum stint length is once again in place this season, with the limit this time set at 27 laps per set of tyres. The latter was based on Pirelli's pre-event simulations, but in practice, the situation is proving even more extreme than expected, as Pirelli's chief engineer Simone Berra explained. “The point is that the graining level and the wear level are higher than what we expected pre-event. It's quite impressive, the surprises that this circuit gives us every time we come here,” Berra smiled. “What we have noticed is that during the high fuel running, the graining is on all three compounds, C3, C2 and C1. C1 is slightly more resilient in terms of mechanical resistance and the graining level is slightly reduced, while on C2 and C3 the graining level is moderate to heavy. “That is accelerating the wear, mainly in two regions: the TWI 2 and 3 area, so basically towards the inside shoulder of the tyre, and then on the very outside shoulder of the tyre as well. We have two points of high wear and we have seen cases of 100% wear already during the high fuel running after 15 laps.” Those cases of extreme localised wear occurred well before the prescribed 27-lap limit, meaning Pirelli is evaluating whether that limit needs to be reduced further. However, the answer is not necessarily yes, given that, in addition to the wear, tyre degradation is also proving higher than expected. “We are evaluating all the sets that we have selected from FP1 and FP2. We are going to check them, to section them, and obviously if there is no integrity issue, we will keep the 27 laps. We know that the graining level will reduce for the race and the teams will do much more management to extend the stint length,” Berra explained. “So, if they don't induce any increase in terms of integrity issues, then we can keep the 27 laps. But it's an analysis that is ongoing in our laboratory, so we are going to understand if we continue with 27 or not.” Pirelli team Pirelli team Higher degradation could make the existing limit less of a concern for Pirelli, as Berra does not expect teams to push right up to the permitted limit of 27 laps per set. item.title: Bruno Fernandes replacement? Mauricio Pochettino turns to Man Utd's forgotten French wonderkid as injury crisis deepens ahead of Old Trafford debut
item.description: Enzo Kana-Biyik Manchester United - Getty Mauricio Pochettino is wasting no time in exploring the depth of his Manchester United squad as he prepares for his first Premier League home game at Old Trafford. With several senior stars sidelined, the Argentine coach has turned to the club's youth ranks to bolster his options for the visit of Brentford. Pochettino promotes academy prospects for Friday training Enzo Kana-Biyik joined Manchester United's senior group for Friday's training session as head coach Pochettino dealt with multiple absences ahead of Saturday's Premier League fixture against Brentford. The 19-year-old French forward trained alongside fellow academy prospects Jack Fletcher, Tyler Fletcher, Jim Thwaites, and Jaydan Kamason. Captain Bruno Fernandes sat out the session through illness , adding to a growing unavailable list that already includes Benjamin Sesko, Marcus Rashford, Carlos Baleba, and Manuel Ugarte. Pochettino did receive one welcome boost, however, with defender Leny Yoro cleared to play after his red card against Liverpool was overturned on appeal. Fernandes faces late fitness check over Portugal virus Speaking at his pre-match press conference, Pochettino confirmed that Fernandes is a doubt for the visit of the Bees after picking up a virus while away with Portugal. The United boss stressed he will assess the midfielder's condition before making a final decision. "Yes, we don't know," Pochettino said. "He's affected by a virus from Portugal. He finished the game a little bit with a problem, and, today, he cannot be part of the training session. "We'll see. We are going to see during the day and tomorrow, how he wakes up, and we'll see. We're not going to take any risks, because you know when this type of situation happens, you don't feel [you can]. "We are going to pay attention but, still, we decide nothing." Kana-Biyik's long road from Le Havre to Old Trafford Kana-Biyik's promotion marks a notable step in his development at the club. United agreed a free transfer to sign the teenage striker from French side Le Havre in April 2025 before officially completing the move that July. Supporters are still waiting to see him make his senior debut, as United immediately loaned him to INEOS-owned Swiss club Lausanne-Sport to gain experience. He scored once in 26 appearances across all competitions there before returning to Manchester, where he has made four U-21 outings this season. Given Pochettino's track record of trusting young players, a first-team call-up could soon follow. Without a top-flight victory since August, the Red Devils are aiming to repeat the result of their last meeting with Brentford and hand Pochettino a winning home debut. item.title: Jazz Chisholm Jr. drew interest from Phillies before joining Blue Jays
item.description: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images Jazz Chisholm Jr. drew interest from Phillies before joining Blue Jays appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia Phillies were reportedly interested in Jazz Chisholm Jr. before the infielder ultimately agreed to a contract with the Toronto Blue Jays . The two-time All-Star ultimately signed a one-year, $20 million deal with Toronto that includes options for the future. According to MLB insider Robert Murray, the Phillies and San Diego Padres were among the teams interested in Chisholm before he chose the Blue Jays. The contract includes a $6 million signing bonus, a $12.5 million salary for 2027, and a $16 million player option with a $1.5 million buyout. It will become a $40 million club option if Chisholm decides to decline the player option. Chisholm is coming off a relatively underwhelming season with the New York Yankees. He hit .231 with 19 home runs, 55 RBIs and a .711 OPS while stealing a career-high 41 bases. However, his 2025 campaign was considerably stronger, as he finished with 31 home runs, 80 RBIs and an .813 OPS. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Phillies could have explored Chisholm as an infield or outfield option. However, his natural position is second base, where Philadelphia already has Bryson Stott. Chisholm also has experience in the outfield but struggled defensively in center field during his time with the Miami Marlins and Yankees. Philadelphia manager Don Mattingly also has experience working with Chisholm, having managed him in Miami from 2020 to 2022. Mattingly previously praised the infielder’s confidence and approach at the plate. “Jazz is Jazz. He’s himself,” Mattingly said in 2024. “I love Jazz just from the standpoint of I think he’s fearless. I don’t think he’s afraid of anybody out there at the plate.” However, the Phillies have yet to make a major league signing this offseason. With Chisholm now off the market, Philadelphia will have to explore other options as it looks to strengthen its lineup ahead of the 2027 season. item.title: Real Madrid could yet welcome back former academy star as future remains undecided
item.description: Real Madrid could yet welcome back former academy star as future remains undecided Nico Paz remains one of the talk of the town in the world of football, and his start to the new season with Como has been absolutely phenomenal. A Real Madrid academy star for a long time, the player left the club looking for regular minutes and found a convenient project to pioneer under Cesc Fabregas in Serie A. His growth at the club has been astronomical; Real Madrid have monitored his situation closely. The club are seriously considering triggering their buy-back clause on him next summer regardless of the cost, but recent reports have highlighted that Paz is still not convinced about the role he will have under Jose Mourinho. Decision not made Paz has not ruled out a Real Madrid return. (Photo by Simone Arveda/Getty Images) As opposed to reports earlier in the week that Paz is against a return , Fabrizio Romano now reports and ‘guarantees’ that the player has not yet made his final decision. The player wants to understand Real Madrid’s plans, project and where they see him fitting into the puzzle before he makes a binding decision. He has not yet decided to officially close the door for Real Madrid, and everything will depend on what the club transmit to him. As matters stand, there is still a chance that Paz will arrive in Madrid next summer. A valid concern The directness with which Paz has handled his career decisions so far is inspiring, for he never allowed the allure of playing for Real Madrid to affect his development. All Nico Paz asks for is a guarantee for minutes. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Throughout his journey, the player’s priority has been regular minutes – something which he earned in abundance on loan and furthered his development. As the door to return to Real Madrid opens one last time, he still continues to approach the situation pragmatically and is asking all the right questions. With Jude Bellingham and Arda Guler already providing in-house solutions for Real Madrid’s attacking midfield, there is seemingly no place for Paz to fit into the XI. If Real Madrid indeed wish to bring Paz back, that is the problem they must look to solve. After all, the player has been open to a return for a long time, and it is only the lack of guaranteed playing time that has inhibited the transfer.

item.title: Relief for Barça Atletic as key duo return in time for top-spot clash against Terrassa
item.description: Relief for Barça Atletic as key duo return in time for top-spot clash against Terrassa Barça Atletic have received a timely boost ahead of Saturday’s crucial Segunda RFEF meeting with Terrassa, with Hamza Abdelkarim and Pedro Villar recovering from injuries and expected to return to the squad, reports Mundo Deportivo . Notably, the match at the Estadi Johan Cruyff carries major significance in the Group 2 promotion race. Barça Atletic currently lead the standings by two points, but their preparations have been complicated by an extensive injury list that has left 11 players unavailable. With the reserve side facing one of their most demanding fixtures of the season, the return of two young players gives coach Juliano Belletti additional options at a critical moment. Hamza Abdelkarim and Pedro Villar return from injury Abdelkarim, 18, has recovered from muscle discomfort that kept him out for the past two weeks. Hamza Abdelkarim’s recovery will be great news for the youth team. (Photo by Daniela Porcelli/Getty Images) The Egyptian striker has had limited opportunities with Barça Atletic this season because of his involvement in the first-team set-up, making Saturday’s fixture an important chance to gain further experience. Hamza has made just one appearance for the reserve side so far, scoring a penalty in their 2-1 victory over Utebo. His return could provide Belletti with a strong attacking option against a Terrassa team chasing the top position. Pedro Villar, meanwhile, has also completed his recovery after spending two months out with an injury to the biceps femoris in his left leg. The 18-year-old central midfielder had featured in four matches before suffering the injury during the 4-0 win over Pena Sport. Pedro Villar will be available against Terrassa. (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) Both players have trained without problems in the build-up to Terrassa’s visit and are expected to be included in the squad. Their exact minutes remain uncertain, particularly after their respective spells on the sidelines. Belletti faces selection challenge with 11 players unavailable The return of Hamza and Villar comes as Barça Atletic continue to deal with a significant injury crisis. On that note, the aforementioned outlet confirms Sama Nomoko, Patricio Pacífico, Juan Hernández, Eder Aller, Shane Kluivert, Ibrahim Diarra, Dani Ávila, Juwensley Onstein, Hafiz Gariba, Josué Caicedo and Mirza Catovic remain unavailable. The number of absentees leaves Belletti with limited room to rotate, particularly in a fixture where the result could have a direct impact on the group’s leadership.

item.title: Patriots' A.J. Brown Injury Leaves Tommy DeVito in Difficult Position
item.description: Patriots' A.J. Brown Injury Leaves Tommy DeVito in Difficult Position originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Patriots ' offense has drawn plenty of attention, and it doesn't look like it's going to change anytime soon. Both A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs have been ruled out against the Chargers, and with Tommy DeVito as the starter due to Drake Maye's injury, that creates some problems. Obviously, Brown has struggled this season, but there's still reason to believe he can be a difference-maker for this organization. One could even argue that when Brown is at his best, he's one of the best five receivers in the game. Unfortunately, that hasn't been the case this year, but it's still better when he's on the field rather than off of it. Any quarterback would struggle without his top two receivers, and while the Chargers have been one of the worst teams in the NFL this season, much of it isn't because of how bad their defense is. A lot of the issues have been rather obvious, too, with the offense not getting enough from the backcourt. He’s got an unreliable 3-point shot as it is and is coming off an Achilles tear at age 30, which makes his durability this year far from a sure thing. "Throw in a $32.7 million salary and it’s hard to find a way to get him on this roster. He’s not an upgrade over Derrick White or Payton Pritchard so I can’t really envision fitting him into this roster given his price tag,” Brian Robb of MassLive wrote . Murray isn't a bad player at this stage of his career, but he isn't what he once was, and asking him to come in and be the player Boston needs now would be a bit questionable. item.description: “It’s not bad getting a compliment like that" – Bischof on Gerrard praise Tom Bischof has been pushed into a prominent role this season under Vincent Kompany and has been making waves both in Germany and abroad. The 21-year-old put in a top performance in October as a rotated Bayern side earned a 2-2 draw with Arsenal. “It was a great game," Bischof said in an interview with the DFL. "If we’d won it in the end, it would’ve been an even greater game. But it was also cool for me to see and to start at such a top level." Bischof completed 96% of his 54 passes against Mikel Arteta's side while also covering the most distance of any player on the pitch. Bischof and Aleksandar Pavlović held their own against a top midfield consisting of Declan Rice and Bruno Guimarães. After the match, the duo earned praise from legendary Liverpool midfielder Steven Gerrard for their performances, with the ex-England international stating he was “really impressed” by both. The praise has not gone unnoticed. “My friends sent it to me and I was obviously aware of it and read it a couple of times, because it makes you happy and is a proud moment having that feeling," Bischof said. "So you’re always happy about it.” Gerrard is not the only Liverpool legend that Bischof has impressed. The youngster has been a regular under new coach Jürgen Klopp for Germany, appearing in four consecutive matches. Germany has won three of the four. “I think he’s just like you expect – the way he gets players on board,” Bischof said. “I’m very convinced of him and think he’ll lead us down a good path.” With Bayern depleted by injuries, and Germany looking to refresh the squad, the 21-year-old should continue to get ample opportunities for both. Still, while on an individual level, he is having a strong season, but there is more work to be done. Bayern are heading into their final six matches of 2026 in mixed form. Among those is a rematch with TSG Hoffenheim, the club where Bischof got his start. Much has changed since he left Hoffenheim in 2025, and the midfielder has gone from strength to strength. Even with Bischof now performing in the Champions League at Bayern, he's looking to continue improving. “It’s not bad getting a compliment like that from Steven Gerrard,” Bischof said. "It makes me happy, but I want to build on my performance from that game and just keep going.”

item.description: San Antonio Spurs forward Victor Wembanyama (1) embraces San Antonio Spurs forward Carter Bryant (11) in an NBA Cup game at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas on Friday, Nov. 27, 2026. The Spurs defeated the Lakers 99-96. (Katina Zentz/San Antonio Express-News) With the Spurs in the throes of one of their most thrilling comebacks of the season, the ball found Stephon Castle in the left corner late Friday night. He didn't need much time to decide what to do with it. "I'm just trying to get the best shot available," Castle said. As it turned out, the best shot available was the one in his hands. Castle's corner 3-pointer with 43.4 seconds remaining gave the Spurs some much-needed breathing room in what became a 99-96 victory over the Los Angeles Lakers in a do-or-die NBA Cup showdown at the Frost Bank Center. "I had the shot," Castle said, "so I took it." Castle and Victor Wembanyama teamed up to win an MVP-caliber duel against Luka Doncic and the Los Angeles Lakers, one that punched the Spurs ticket into the NBA Cup knockout rounds. The Spurs face Dallas on Friday at the American Airlines Center. Getting there required the Spurs to dig themselves out of a hole they had spent the first half making. Castle finished with 26 points - including a late 3-pointer that put the Spurs ahead 96-90 - while Wembanyama piled up 25 points, 16 rebounds, two blocks and four steals. San Antonio Spurs guard Stephon Castle (5) hits a drum after the team defeated the Los Angeles Lakers 99-96 in an NBA Cup game at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas on Friday, Nov. 27, 2026. (Katina Zentz/San Antonio Express-News) Doncic cooled after a sizzling start, ending with 31 points but needing 31 shot attempts to get there. Playing in his first game since suffering a heel injury Nov. 11, Austin Reaves rejoined the L.A. lineup and chipped in 21 points. To stay alive in the NBA Cup field, the Spurs had to overcome their worst first quarter (14 points) and first half (38 points) of the season. The Spurs fell behind by as many as 20 points before intermission. "We got punked in the first half," Spurs forward Carter Bryant said. The Spurs trimmed their deficit to 58-34 at the break, then turned the tables on the Lakers after halftime. A 30-14 third quarter pulled the Spurs into a 68-all tie headed to the fourth, where they did just enough to pull out the victory. "We might have been dominated in the first half," Wembanyama said. "We dominated more than they did in the second half." The Spurs improved to 16-4, surpassing the Lakers (15-4) for the top record in the Western Conference. item.title: Inside story of how Marc Casado’s loan move from Barcelona to Deportivo was pulled off on deadline day
item.description: Inside story of how Marc Casado’s loan move from Barcelona to Deportivo was pulled off on deadline day Barcelona had decided last summer that Marc Casado needed to leave in search of regular football, but the club initially preferred a permanent transfer rather than a loan. This is because the midfielder attracted financially attractive offers from Saudi Arabia and interest from Turkish clubs, yet he prioritised continuing his career in Spain and remaining in European football. Furthermore, the Blaugrana’s €30 million valuation proved a major obstacle, but that was understandable because Casado still had two years left on his contract and was reluctant to sever his connection with the club where he had developed since joining La Masia in 2016. Notably, Deportivo’s proposal only gained momentum late in the window . The La Liga club’s ambitious project, including the arrivals of former Barcelona players Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang and Adama Traore, appealed to Casado, who was keen to find a sporting environment where he could play regularly. Deportivo’s late approach nearly collapsed Deportivo have a non-mandatory €30 million purchase option for Marc Casado. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) According to SPORT , Deportivo moved quickly enough to arrange a flight for Casado to A Coruna, but the midfielder remained in Barcelona after disagreements between the clubs prevented the deal from being completed. The negotiations continued into the final day of the transfer window. Barcelona wanted to protect their financial interests, while Deportivo needed an agreement that could fit within its economic limitations. Casado’s representative, Jorge Mendes, and the clubs’ legal teams remained involved as the parties worked through the final details. The result was a season-long loan with a non-mandatory €30 million purchase option, giving Deportivo the opportunity to sign him permanently without an obligation to do so. The agreement was completed five minutes before the deadline Deportivo wasn’t the most favourable transfer for Casado. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) As per the outlet, the verbal agreement between Barcelona and Deportivo was reached at approximately 11pm. The remaining legal procedures were completed electronically, allowing Casado to be registered just five minutes before the transfer window closed. Barcelona’s official announcement confirmed that the midfielder would spend the season at Deportivo until June 30, 2027. Put together, the late agreement was a compromise for all parties , as Barcelona avoided losing the player without a transfer arrangement, Deportivo secured a midfielder for its return to the top flight, and Casado found a route to regular football while keeping the possibility of returning to his boyhood club open.

item.title: 'We must improve quickly!' - Jordan Henderson lays blame on 'sloppy' Chelsea stars after Nottingham Forest defensive horror show
item.description: Nottingham Forest FC v Chelsea FC - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Jordan Henderson has delivered a scathing assessment of Chelsea’s defensive standards following their disappointing 3-2 defeat to Nottingham Forest. The veteran midfielder insisted the Blues were the architects of their own downfall at the City Ground as they struggled to maintain concentration against their hosts. Slow starts cost Blues at the City Ground Nottingham Forest punished Chelsea inside the opening five minutes of both halves, leaving the visitors chasing deficits of 2-0 and 3-1 before they found any attacking rhythm. Emmanuel Emegha struck twice to spark a late fightback as Forest dropped deeper to protect their lead, yet the Blues ran out of time to rescue a point . Henderson laments preventable goals and late urgency Speaking after the final whistle, Henderson did not hide his frustration over how easily Forest breached Chelsea's backline early in each period. "The goals we conceded were sloppy," the former Liverpool captain told Chelsea's official website . "We are disappointed with that first and foremost. I think the three goals we can stop them, so we are really disappointed with that. "For some reason they had a couple of half-decent chances, and they scored. The first five minutes of the first half, the first five minutes of the second half, so we are disappointed with the goals we have conceded for sure." The veteran midfielder also noted that Chelsea only showed real urgency once Forest retreated to defend their cushion. He added: "We didn't get going until they were 2-0 up or 3-1 up, when they started to drop deep and we started to get the ball forward a bit quicker. "Obviously we kept going and we got a couple of goals. We were pushing in the last few minutes of the game to try and get an equaliser. We kept going right until the end, which was a positive, but overall we can still play better and be better. Defensively, we need to improve quickly." Whole squad must share defensive burden Rather than singling out the backline, Henderson framed the defeat as a collective failure, warning that lapses in concentration have become a recurring problem across the side. item.description: BVB striker Fábio Silva discusses secret behind good form and friendship with Guirassy Fábio Silva revealed the reasons behind his excellent start to the new campaign in an exclusive interview with Bundesliga. The 24-year-old was the latest guest in DFL’s “Midweek Interviews” segment. “I'm enjoying myself a lot,” the Portuguese U21 international said about his current form. “I think everyone can see the way I'm happy playing for this club, the joy I have playing with everyone when I'm on the pitch. You play for this club, for the fans. And, of course, it's important to have people behind me because I'm here to help this club to win titles.” Fábio Silva already scored more goals (3) than his debut season (2), while he also added two assists to his name in nine Bundesliga appearances. He also found the net in the Franz Beckenbauer Supercup, DFB-Pokal and the UEFA Champions League. “It's always important to score. I'm not saying it's the most important thing. I want to score every game, but I think as well that everyone can see I can do a lot of things to help the team with other parts of the game as well.” he told Bundesliga. As he has done in previous interviews, the former journeyman explained how difficult it is for players to sit on the bench. “Every player wants to play every game and start every game. If someone says the opposite, he’s lying, because everyone wants to be involved and play. “But the coach speaks a lot with me. I speak a lot with the coach, and he always tries to give me motivation. If I don't start, he always comes to me and says I can be important for the team. And everyone can see as well. I always try to focus on what I can control. I cannot control what's going to be the line-up. This depends on the coach. What I can control is to do my best in training, show the coach I'm ready. And whenever he wants, I'm going to be always there to try to help the club and my teammates.” Despite his outspoken character when it comes to playing time, the striker has a very good relationship with BVB's star striker Serhou Guirassy. The Guinean spoke highly of his competitor in previous interviews, and the same is the case for Fábio Silva. “I think we speak the same football. Sometimes we don't even speak before the games. I know what he's thinking. He knows what I think. I know what he needs in the game because I play in his position. And so I understand. “Of course, that helps outside the pitch as well, because I think he's one of the closest persons I have in the dressing room. He's an experienced guy. He played a lot of games in his career. So, he helped me a lot. Even last season, when I didn't play and wasn’t feeling so good, he always came to me in training, and tried to help me. So, he is one of the important players here in Dortmund. And everyone can see when I play with him, I think I play better. And when he plays with me, I think he plays better as well.”

item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 20: Head coach Kate Paye of the Stanford Cardinal reacts during the first half against the Washington Huskies at Alaska Airlines Arena on November 20, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Getty The Stanford Cardinal are one of the proudest women’s college basketball programs in existence. That’s not who the Cardinal are right now, though. They’ve lost three games in a row, and on Friday night, they lost by 23 points to Columbia out of the Ivy League. No offense at all to Columbia, but this isn’t a game Stanford of yesteryear even comes close to losing. Stanford is now 4-4 on the young season. The Cardinal lost by 15 in their opener to Arizona. They then rattled off four wins in a row: St. Mary’s, UC-Davis, Santa Clara and Gonzaga. Since then, Stanford has lost 105-50 to No. 16 Washington, 73-62 to Portland and 68-45 to Columbia. There’s no rest for the wicked as they play San Diego State on Saturday and Hawaii on Sunday. It’s a massive fall from grace, and Kate Paye’s job could be in trouble. Kate Paye Firing Calls It’s not clear how abrupt Stanford would be with firing a women’s basketball coach, but there are certainly calls for it to happen. One commentor on X wrote: “No one has ever been more fired than Kate Paye is right now. Aaron Rodgers during the Pat McAfee interview was less fired than Coach Paye is now.” Another wrote: “What the what?!” And a third : “That’s it. That seals the deal. I’m no longer a Stanford WBB fan. item.title: Ranking the Premier League's ultimate free-kick specialists
item.description: [BBC] Dip, swerve, curl, whip. Hours spent mastering the craft of a great free-kick ensure those that ripple the back of the net are particularly satisfying. This week we are digging into the Premier League's all-time best takers. The number of goals scored from direct free-kicks has gradually decreased over the past two decades (boo!) with a rising focus on generating higher-quality chances, rather than having a pop from range. It is perhaps unsurprising then that James Maddison is the only current player in the competition's all-time top 25 free-kick scorers, after James Ward-Prowse returned to Championship side Southampton in the summer. Dominik Szoboszlai, however, is bucking the trend with five since joining Liverpool from 32 attempts - an impressive conversion rate of 15.6% and almost a third of his total Premier League goals. He looks on course to become a free-kick great, already only one goal behind Trent Alexander-Arnold and Leighton Baines and just two off the likes of Matt le Tissier, Wayne Rooney and Steven Gerrard. The majority of top scorers hail from the halcyon era of, essentially, having a dig. Yaya Toure belongs in another category - he misses out on the top 10 below but could be deemed a 'one-season wonder' in this realm, despite having eight years at Manchester City. His prolific spell in 2013-14 deserves recognition, scoring four of his seven free-kick attempts that term - a staggering 57.1% conversion rate and by far the Premier League's best since Opta began collecting such data in 2006. There is also an honourable mention for Louis Saha, the only man in the Premier League era to score a free-kick with each foot - with his left for Manchester United against Southampton in January 2004, and with his right for Everton against Fulham seven years later. And while we are here, these are the goalkeepers who least liked facing them. What we are looking for, though, are the real free-kick specialists - those players whose names evoke memories of ball meeting top bins. For that reason, despite sitting joint-third on the scorers list with 12, Cristiano Ronaldo and Thierry Henry do not make it. They just scored too many goals - and too many great ones - to be renowned specifically for their set-pieces. Fewer than 7% of Henry's 175 Premier League goals were free-kicks, netting one on average every 21.5 games. Ronaldo, meanwhile, tried his luck 167 times, scoring one roughly every 14 attempts. So let's get stuck into the top 10. The first spot up for grabs could have gone several ways - Maddison, as mentioned, has a decent shout to be included, and likewise Christian Eriksen who netted eight in the Premier League and also laid on 13 free-kick assists. Frank Lampard has nine goals but also the most attempts on record - and the data only accounts for half his Premier League career. Instead, I've gone for... The league again sat out the holiday, while the NFL scheduled three games and opened the week with its first Thanksgiving Eve game. Richard Jefferson made the pitch on Wednesday’s episode of the “Road Trippin’ Show.” The 2016 NBA champion framed a return to Thanksgiving as the league’s answer to the NFL’s Christmas Day games, but fans doubted basketball could compete with the Goliath market of football for viewers. Fans Push Back Against Richard Jefferson’s Case for NBA Games on Thanksgiving The panel was asked whether the NBA should bring back Thanksgiving games. Jefferson’s co-hosts, Channing Frye and Kendrick Perkins, both came out against it, and Perkins called Thanksgiving his “favorite holiday.” Jefferson, a 17-year NBA veteran, took the other side and aimed his response squarely at the NFL, which has made Christmas Day games a regular part of its schedule since 2020. “They should bring back Thanksgiving games. Why? Because the NFL disrespected us and started to have games on Christmas Day and take our audience. Christmas Day belongs to us. If y’all want to play that game, then let’s start playing hoop games,” Jefferson said. Jefferson also made a practical case for the idea. “So now all of a sudden, when you’re watching … whoever versus whoever and the score is 42-7, … you can switch the channel and turn on a basketball game.” READ MORE: ‘The NFL Disrespected Us,’ ‘If Y’all Want To Play That Game’ — Richard Jefferson Urges NBA To Retaliate in Holiday TV Ratings Battle The NBA has not played on Thanksgiving since 2010. One user proposed a truce, writing , “NFL keeps Thanksgiving, NBA keeps Christmas, and we all shut up.” Others doubted the NBA’s chances in a direct matchup. As one fan put it , “NFL owns the NBA. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
